column1: # The tariqs applications actually name — طرق الأداء المشهورة.
# `tariq` is the concept and has its dictionary entry: the path of transmission
# below the rawi. Al-Nashr names some 980 of them for the 10 readings, and that
# enumeration is not here (the note at the head of registries/qiraat.tsv says
# what was tried and why it was not kept). This registry is the narrower thing
# an application stores: a Hafs recording or a Mushaf is labelled «من طريق
# الشاطبية» or «من طريق طيبة النشر», and the lengths of madd and the ghunnah
# follow that label. Four named routes cover what is stored in practice.
# A ROUTE NAMED AFTER A BOOK IS STILL A ROUTE
# Each of the four is a book, and the reading is said to be «من طريق» that book:
# the book fixes which of the paths below the rawi are being followed, and the
# name of the book has become the name of that path. That is the sense the
# dictionary's `tariq` entry gives — a finer level than the riwayah that tells
# paths of delivery apart — and it is the sense a recording's label carries. So
# the rows are filed under `tariq`, and `kind` says what each one is a route of.
# `covers` names the readings the book transmits: the seven (al-Shatibiyyah,
# al-Taysir), the three that complete the ten (al-Durrah), or all ten
# (Tayyibat al-Nashr). `qiraat` lists them as codes in registries/qiraat.tsv.
# THE CODES ARE DERIVED
# A book's title is a word with a meaning, so it is derived from its Arabic by
# tools/translit.py like every other term (section 13: only a person's name is
# exempt). `alternative_spellings` carries the forms in use.
# `ref` cites al-Nashr, ed. al-Dabba, as volume/page: 1/58 is where Ibn al-Jazari
# lists al-Taysir among the works he transmits from, and 1/61 al-Shatibiyyah.
# Al-Durrah and al-Tayyibah are his own later works and al-Nashr does not cite
# them; the editor's introduction names both among his writings, and
# `muqaddimah/7` is that page.
# code
shatibiyyah
tayyibat_al_nashr
durrah
taysir
